Patterns from your own data and published research. Not medical advice — you decide, ideally with your diabetes team.

Sukoon looks for patterns in your readings and logbook and compares them with published clinical targets and formulas. It doesn\'t diagnose or prescribe, it doesn\'t know your whole situation, and it can be wrong — sensors drift and logs miss things.\n\nNothing here tells you to change a dose. Any change to insulin, food or activity is your own decision and responsibility, ideally made with your diabetes team. If you feel unwell or you\'re low, treat first and get help.
OFTEN DISCUSSED WITH YOUR CARE TEAM

This \"dawn phenomenon\" comes from early-morning hormones. It\'s commonly discussed with the timing or amount of basal insulin.

Rapid insulin keeps working for 3–5 hours, so overlapping doses add up (\"stacking\"). Many people check how much insulin is still active before a correction.

Tap a topic to open it. Everything here is also where you would look for it in the app.

You → Your sensor → Connect sensor, then hold the top of the phone against the sensor until it buzzes. Sukoon reads its memory (the last 8 hours appear at once) and takes over its Bluetooth stream; live readings arrive every minute. “Check sensor” only reads it without taking it over. Another app (like DiaBox) can take the sensor back with its own scan, and a new tap in Sukoon takes it back again.

The big number is your latest reading, with an arrow for where it\'s heading. A reading older than 10 minutes is greyed out and never shown as current. A new sensor needs an hour to warm up, and in its last day a banner tells you when it stops. The icons at the top log food and insulin; “u active” is rapid insulin that\'s still working.

Urgent low (under 55) is always on: it takes over the screen and keeps sounding until you answer it. Low, going-low, high and no-signal alarms are set in You → Alarms, each with its own sound (a phone sound or your own file). Tap Test to hear the urgent alarm. Allow everything in You → Setup so alarms get through silent mode and Do Not Disturb.

If an urgent low, or a lost signal while you were low, gets no answer for the time you choose, Sukoon counts down 60 seconds on screen, then texts everyone in You → Emergency contacts and calls the first one. Tap I\'m OK at any time to stop it. The text can include a map link. On Now, “Alert my emergency contact” lets you text, WhatsApp or call them yourself.

Trends → Logbook holds meals, rapid and basal insulin, finger-pricks, activity and notes. A meal can carry the insulin you took for it and how many minutes before eating. Each entry shows your glucose at that moment; a finger-prick shows how far the sensor was from your meter. The AI can estimate a meal\'s carbs from a photo or a description, but it never suggests doses.

The graph shows any range from 3 hours to 14 days, with time in range and GMI (an A1C estimate), and every reading listed below it. Insights finds patterns, like recurring lows at a certain hour, and says where each rule comes from; nothing there is an instruction. Report gives the one-page AGP summary clinics use, with a PDF to share.
Add a Sukoon widget from your home screen\'s widget list, or from You → Home-screen widgets. Resize it from one cell to half the screen; tap Edit to choose its graph and details.

Make an account in You → Sharing; “Invite someone to follow you” sends a one-time code (valid 24 hours). They enter it in their Sukoon and see your readings live, with alerts if they want them. You can remove a follower at any time. Only real sensor readings are shared.

Nightscout: Sukoon uploads readings and logbook entries to your own Nightscout site. Your data: export everything as a CSV file. Health Connect: meals from MyFitnessPal come into the Logbook, and your readings go out for other apps.

Off by default, because the sensor\'s factory calibration is usually best. When on, Sukoon nudges readings toward your recent finger-pricks taken while your glucose was steady, within strict limits, and it never raises a low reading.

Sukoon keeps a small notification showing your glucose; that is what keeps the sensor connection alive. Let it ignore battery optimization, and on Samsung or Xiaomi phones open the extra background settings in You → Setup. After a restart or an update it reconnects by itself.

Sukoon is not a medical device. If a reading doesn\'t match how you feel, check with a finger-prick, and follow your care team\'s advice on treatment. In an emergency, call your local emergency number.
